title: What may be, must be or may have been: epistemic modality

sections.title: Clauses for what may be true
sections.content: You know *feltehetőleg* and *nem zárható ki, hogy* from C1 Unit 3. This lesson teaches the clauses that say what may be, must be or may have been true: *könnyen meglehet, hogy* (it may well be that), *nem kizárt, hogy* (it is not out of the question that), *számolni kell azzal, hogy* (one has to reckon with the fact that) and *aligha képzelhető el, hogy ne* (it is hardly conceivable that ... not).

sections.title: Must have been and might have been
sections.content: Example: *Könnyen meglehet, hogy a nyelvmodellek hamarosan sok szöveget írnak, és számolni kell azzal, hogy a gép is téved.* For the past, two patterns say that something must have been true. *Kellett, hogy* + subjunctive: *Már kellett, hogy lássa* (he or she must have seen it already); *kell, hogy legyen* is the present: *Kell, hogy legyen más magyarázat* (there must be another explanation). A modal verb can also carry the guess: *Valakinek tudnia kellett a hibáról* (someone must have known about the error). To say it might have happened, use *-hatott/-hetett*: *Elveszhetett a levél* (the letter may have got lost). Do not mix it up with *-hatott volna* (B1 Unit 20, *lehetett volna*), which says that it could have happened but did not: *Elveszhetett volna a levél, de megtalálták.*

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: Könnyen meglehet, hogy a gép hamarosan sok szöveget ír.
It may well be that the machine will soon write many texts.
Nem kizárt, hogy a program hibázik.
It is not out of the question that the program makes mistakes.
Valakinek tudnia kellett a hibáról. Már kellett, hogy lássa.
Someone must have known about the error. He or she must have seen it already.
